logic_errors.description: The Float64 losslessness guard converts back to the input integer dtype and uses array_equal. On the required macOS arm64 NumPy 2.1.3 runtime, an out-of-range Float64 value can saturate back to that dtype's maximum, so this check passes even though the stored Float64 is a different integer. write_raw then succeeds and read_raw returns the changed number.
logic_errors.evidence: Fresh production write_raw/read_raw calls with an in-memory NPZ transport reproduced both silent +1 changes. File opening/loading/hash functions were redirected only for an absent scratch sentinel; actual validation, packing, numeric serialization, array validation and reconstruction executed. No source or on-disk raw file was changed. Confirmatory probe exited 0 after asserting both mismatches; the initial expectation-of-losslessness probe exited 1 on the actual defect. Separate 11-case integer probes distinguished representable positive controls from rejected nonrepresentable values and these two false acceptances.
logic_errors.impact: Violates required exact raw preservation and allows a corrupted raw observation to pass digest/schema readback. Normalized-output equality does not catch face-only loss because face is excluded from hm153; both examples retained equal pack_frame outputs. This does not demonstrate corruption of the actual SDK Float64 outputs or any real FSL source.
logic_errors.requested_change: Use a genuinely exact value/representability test that cannot be satisfied by saturating integer cast-back. Retain valid representable integers and Float64 SDK values; add signed/unsigned extrema regressions asserting rejection before publication and compare raw numeric values using exact scalar semantics, not mixed float/integer NumPy equality. Re-review the full affected codec/test/documentation scope with refreshed bindings; do not weaken the lossless contract.
logic_errors.reproduction_note: The supplied red-capable reproduction stops at the first violated invariant. The actual confirmatory run evaluated both types and asserted actual == input + 1, recording both outcomes.
